figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Key steps and clinical studies used in PBPK model building, validation, and application. All clinical studies and simulations were done in healthy participants. CL iv, intravenous clearance; CsA, cyclosporine A; DDI, drug–drug interaction; fe, fraction of drug excreted; f m, fraction of drug metabolized; f m,CYP3A4, fraction of drug metabolized by cytochrome P450 3A4; HLM, human liver microsomes; IN, intranasal; IV, intravenous; MD, multiple dose; OATP1B3, organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B3; PBPK, physiologically based pharmacokinetic; P‐gp, P‐glycoprotein; QD, once daily; rCYP, recombinant cytochrome P450; SD, single dose; V ss, volume of distribution at steady state.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Simulated and observed zavegepant concentration–time profiles (model development) following a single oral dose of zavegepant administered alone and with MD itraconazole (a) or MD rifampin (b). Gray lines represent mean zavegepant concentrations of the simulated individual trials, and black lines represent mean concentration for the simulated population (n = 180 for a; n = 150 for b). Circles and triangles represent observed mean zavegepant concentrations (n = 18 for a; n = 15 for b). Solid lines/circles represent zavegepant concentration in the absence of the specified concomitant medication, and dashed lines/triangles represent concentrations in the presence of the concomitant medication. In a, 50 mg zavegepant was administered on the eighth day of 9 days of dosing with 200 mg itraconazole QD (simulations considered the inhibitory effect on CYP3A4, P‐gp, and OATP1B3 by itraconazole and OH‐itraconazole). In b, 100 mg zavegepant was administered on the 10th day of 10 days of dosing with 600 mg rifampin QD. CYP3A4, cytochrome P450 3A4; MD, multiple dose; OATP1B3, organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B3; P‐gp, P‐glycoprotein; QD, once daily.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Simulated and observed zavegepant plasma concentration–time profiles (model validation) following 5 mg IN zavegepant (a), 10 mg IN zavegepant (b), and 10 mg IN zavegepant administered with MD itraconazole (c). Gray lines represent mean zavegepant concentrations of the simulated individual trials, and black lines represent mean concentration for the simulated population (n = 90 for a and b; n = 180 for c). Circles and triangles represent observed mean zavegepant concentrations (n = 9 for a and b; n = 18 for c). In c, solid lines/circles represent zavegepant concentration in the absence of the specified concomitant medication, and dashed lines/triangles represent concentrations in the presence of the concomitant medication. In c, 10 mg IN zavegepant was administered on the fourth day of 9 days of dosing with 200 mg itraconazole QD. IN, intranasal; MD, multiple dose; QD, once daily.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: Observed and predicted DDI effects of CYP3A/P‐gp and OATP1B/NTCP perpetrator drugs on IN and oral zavegepant AUC 0‐inf (a) and C max (b). Datapoints present GMR (90% CI). Dashed vertical lines represent bioequivalence limits of 0.8–1.25. AUC, area under the curve; CI, confidence interval; C max, time to maximum plasma concentration; CYP3A, cytochrome P450 3A; DDI, drug–drug interaction; GMR, geometric mean ratio; IN, intranasal; MD, multiple dose; NTCP, Na+/taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide; OATP1B3, organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B3; P‐gp, P‐glycoprotein.
